module_title: Browser Features and Search Engine Mechanics
introduction: At this intermediate level, we will explore the background technical features of web browsers (Cookies, Cache, History) and the automated methods search engines use to discover data across the internet (Web Crawlers).

core_concepts.title: Cookies
core_concepts.description: When you visit a website (like Amazon), it saves a tiny text file on your computer to remember your preferences (e.g., what you left in your shopping cart, your language choice, or your login session). This tracker file is called a 'Cookie'.

core_concepts.title: Cache Memory (Browser Cache)
core_concepts.description: A temporary storage memory used by your browser. The browser downloads and saves heavy website data (like logos, background images, and formatting scripts) so that the next time you visit that same website, it loads 'significantly faster'.

core_concepts.title: Incognito Mode (Private Browsing)
core_concepts.description: A special privacy mode offered by web browsers. In this mode, the browser does NOT save your browsing 'History', 'Passwords', or 'Cookies' after you close the window. (Shortcut in Chrome: Ctrl + Shift + N).

core_concepts.title: Web Crawlers (Spiders / Bots)
core_concepts.description: Search engines do not magically know everything. They use automated software robots called 'Web Crawlers' or 'Spiders' that constantly roam the internet, jumping from link to link, to discover new websites and 'Index' them into the search engine's massive database.

important_entities.name: Bookmark
important_entities.significance: A browser feature that allows you to save the URL of a favorite webpage so you can access it directly with one click in the future without searching for it again. (Shortcut: Ctrl + D).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants assume these are the same. They are not. 'History' only saves the text names and URLs of the sites you visited (a logbook). 'Cache' saves the actual heavy data files (images, scripts) to save internet bandwidth on your next visit.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The World Wide 'Web' is a giant net, and search engines use automated 'Spiders' (Crawlers) to traverse this net and catch data.

exam_strategy_tips: In statement-based questions, examiners often test the location of Cookies. Remember: 'Cookies' are strictly stored on the User's Computer (Client-side), NOT on the website's main server. This is a favorite Banking IT question.
